arithmetic/add/self-division-plus-consta.reason: CEL carries a NaN or a signed Infinity out of the division and through the arithmetic composed on top of it; SQL has no value that does, because the NULLIF divide-by-zero guard turns the whole sum into NULL. The adapter resolves a non-finite division only where the division IS the comparison operand, so a division nested under further arithmetic fails closed instead of emitting the under-granting filter

The same nested-division limitation as `arithmetic/add/self-division-plus-constant-greater-than`, and the arm that proves it matters: `NaN != 2.0` is TRUE and the PDP allows the zero row, while `NULL + 1 <> 2` is UNKNOWN and drops it

arithmetic/divide/field-by-field.reason: The denominator is a DIFFERENT column, so it may be zero on a row where the numerator is not. CEL divides to a signed Infinity and IEEE-754 keeps the sign of the zero; SQL cannot tell -0.0 from 0.0, and a NULLIF guard collapses both to NULL. The sign of the Infinity decides which side of an order comparison the row falls on, so no guard recovers it and the adapter refuses. A constant denominator, or a column divided by itself, stays translatable

arithmetic/divide/nested-division-diviso.reason: The inner divisor is a column that may be zero; SQL cannot preserve the IEEE signed-zero infinity needed to evaluate the nested division.

arithmetic/multiply/nan-times-zero-plus-.reason: The self-division yields NaN on the zero row, and CEL carries it through `* 0.0 + aDouble`; SQL has no NaN, and the NULLIF divide-by-zero guard would turn the sum into NULL. The adapter resolves a non-finite division only where the division IS the comparison operand, so the multiplication refuses its possibly-NaN operand rather than emit a filter

cast/double/malformed-string.reason: SQL CAST reads a string's leading digits where CEL double() rejects the whole string; double() over a string column is refused.

cast/double/negated-malformed-string.reason: SQL floating-point casts accept malformed string prefixes or coerce them to zero, unlike CEL errors; negation cannot make the conversion safe.

cast/int/malformed-string.reason: SQL CAST reads a string's leading digits where CEL int() rejects the whole string; int() over a string column is refused.

cast/int/negated-malformed-string.reason: SQL numeric casts accept malformed string prefixes or coerce them to zero, unlike CEL errors; negation cannot make the conversion safe.

cast/int/string-beyond-double-precision.reason: SQL CAST reads a string's leading digits where CEL int() rejects the whole string; int() over a string column is refused.

cast/string/from-int-beyond-double-preci.reason: string() wraps int() over a string column, which is refused: CEL reads the whole string or errors, but a SQL CAST reads the leading digits and gives a number.

cast/string/from-integral-ternary.reason: string() over a ternary of whole-number constants is refused: the plan carries 1000000 and 1000000.0 as the same number, and CEL spells the int "1000000" and the double "1e+06", so SQL cannot know which text to produce.

cast/string/from-negative-zero-double.reason: string() over a double column is compared by reading the literal back as the double CEL spells that way; "-0" is -0.0, and SQL (SQLite's REAL, PostgreSQL's and MySQL's DOUBLE) compares -0.0 equal to 0.0, so the filter could not tell i5 from a row holding 0.0. A zero literal is refused

cast/string/negated-from-integral-ternar.reason: Same untyped whole-number ternary under string() as cast/string/from-integral-ternary, under negation.

cast/timestamp/malformed-string.reason: timestamp() over a column holding a formatted string would compare text in SQL, not instants; the attribute must map to a datetime column.

cast/timestamp/negated-malformed-string.reason: The mapper supplies a string column; the adapter only compares instants through native temporal columns, without portable error-preserving parsing of malformed strings.

collection/except/equals-list-literal.reason: The SQL translator has no two-list difference value; the walk refuses except in each arrival position.

collection/exists/map-keys.reason: exists() over the parent ranges over the keys of a map, and the parent is a to-one association, which the adapter refuses as a macro's collection: a subquery over it ranges over rows, and SQL has no way to enumerate which of a row's columns are non-NULL as the map's keys.

collection/exists/negated-map-keys.reason: Same to-one parent read as a map as collection/exists/map-keys, under negation.

collection/index/first-element-of-boolea.reason: Positional access into a list of booleans, the same refusal as `collection/index/first-element-of-string-list`: `index` has no case in the translator's operator dispatch, so the walk falls through to the generic unsupported-operator refusal before the comparison around it is built. `aBoolList` is a one_to_many association mapped by member field, and an association mapping carries no element order, so `aBoolList[0]` names whichever row the engine returns first without an ORDER BY the plan does not carry. A caller whose element table has a position column, as the harness table does, can supply the override the message offers

collection/index/first-element-of-string.reason: Positional access into a scalar list. `index` has no case in the translator's operator dispatch at all, so the walk falls through to the generic unsupported-operator refusal rather than to a leaf-operand guard — which is why the message names the operator and offers an override. A caller whose table has a deterministic ordering column can express it faithfully, and the override the message offers is that escape hatch

timestamp/equals/field-to-field-without-.reason: SQL temporal columns preserve instants but discard the RFC-3339 spelling compared by bare CEL attributes; timestamp wrappers are required.

timestamp/greater-than/relative-window-v.reason: The same sub-microsecond now() literal as `timestamp/less-than/relative-window`, reached with the operands the other way round. Operand order does not change what a Time binds as, so the refusal is the same one

timestamp/less-than/relative-window.reason: The planner folds `now() - duration("24h")` to a literal with nanosecond precision, and Sequel literalizes a Time into SQL at microsecond precision at best — SQLite stores a formatted string and MySQL DATETIME(6) truncates. Rounding the literal compares against a different instant than the policy names, in the direction that admits rows just outside the window, so the adapter refuses rather than move the boundary

type-mismatch/equals/boolean-list-elemen.reason: The cross-type probe `aBoolList[0] == 1 || aNumber == 5`, refused at the `index` in its first disjunct for the same missing element order as `collection/index/first-element-of-boolean-list`, so nothing is emitted for either disjunct. The refusal is also what keeps the cross-type hazard shut on this store: SQLite holds a boolean column as the integer 1, so a positional lowering that compared the stored `aBoolList` element with the literal would return b4 and c1, whose first element is true, where CEL's heterogeneous equality is false for every row

type-mismatch/equals/number-list-element.reason: The cross-type probe `aNumberList[0] == true || aNumber == 5`, refused at the `index` in its first disjunct for the same missing element order as `collection/index/first-element-of-number-list`, so nothing is emitted for either disjunct. The refusal is also what keeps the cross-type hazard shut on this store: SQLite reads the literal TRUE as the integer 1, so a positional lowering that compared the stored `aNumberList` element with the literal would return b4, whose first element is 1, where CEL's heterogeneous equality is false for every row
